newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU flour firms bid for 100,000 T export in France.
newsitem.headline: EU flour firms bid for 100,000 T export in France.

text.p: European flour firms applied through France for some 100,000 tonnes of exports last Thursday with licences carrying a 27 Ecu-per-tonne rebate, France's grain office ONIC said on Monday.
Throughout the EU, flour firms may have bid last week for licences to export more than 400,000 tonnes of flour with a 27 Ecu rebate, industry sources said.
Operators placed their bids before the EU's cereals management committee cut the daily rebate applying to daily flour exports to 22 Ecus per tonne from 27 Ecus.
The Commission has three working days to decide whether to accept or refuse the bids.
The decision to cut the flour rebate was linked to a cut in the refund offered on EU wheat grain exports, as firmer U.S. wheat prices eased pressure for higher EU wheat subsidies.
The flour rebate is usually linked to the wheat rebate. To reach a flour rebate, the wheat figure is usually multiplied by a coefficient of 1.37.

EU soft wheat flour export commitments between July 1 and November 12 were still lagging behind last year at 1.539 million tonnes (flour equivalent) against 1.970 million, the European flour exporters association Euroflour estimated. --Paris newsroom +331 42215432
